title: Scenic Half Marathon Krabi 2026 Review: What the Race Is Like
seo_title: Scenic Half Marathon Krabi 2026 Review | Ao Nang
meta_description: Scenic Half Marathon Krabi review: a World Athletics label half marathon from Ao Nang to Noppharat Thara Beach, won by one second on 13 September 2026.
dek: Krabi's stop on Thailand's Scenic Marathon Series is a half marathon from Ao Nang to Noppharat Thara Beach, with a beach run the day before. Here is what the 2025 and 2026 editions were like.
verdict: The Scenic Half Marathon Krabi is a small-town race with a serious front end. It carries a World Athletics Road Race Label [2], and the 2026 edition, on 13 September, was won by one second: Poland's Krzysztof Hadas in 1:08:57 from Ethiopia's Tsegaye Keress [2]. For everyone else it is a two-day weekend: a short beach run on the Saturday and the 21 km and 10 km road races on the Sunday, starting at the Krabi provincial stadium in Ao Nang and finishing at Noppharat Thara Beach [1]. Expect humidity and a rolling course [2]. It is worth the trip if you want a scenic half marathon at a beach resort, as long as you don't expect a fast time.

sections.heading: How the Weekend Works
paragraphs: In 2025 the event ran over two days. A beach run of 5 km and 3 km was held on Saturday 6 September along the coastal road at Noppharat Thara Beach, and the 21 km and 10 km road runs on Sunday 7 September [1]. The road races started at Krabi Provincial Stadium in Ao Nang and finished at Noppharat Thara Beach National Park [1].

Krabi is one of five stops in the Scenic Marathon Series, and the race is held under the standards of the Athletic Association of Thailand and World Athletics [1]. The title sponsor's village in 2025 included a water tunnel, a cheer zone and a foot-soak station for finishers [1].

sections.heading: The 2026 Race at the Front
paragraphs: The 2026 half marathon was run on 13 September [2]. Krzysztof Hadas of Poland won in 1:08:57, one second ahead of Tsegaye Keress of Ethiopia, with Gemechu Dida of Ethiopia third in 1:09:15 and Kenya's Nicholas Kipchirchir fourth in 1:10:18 [2]. Thailand's Jongjaijit Intouch was fifth in 1:11:04 [2].

The race report describes a dawn start to avoid the heat, high humidity, and a rolling route with hill sections that led the leaders to start cautiously [2]. If athletes running 1:09 were pacing conservatively, most runners should too.

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: If you want to combine a race with a beach holiday, yes. The course runs past the limestone scenery the area is known for, the finish is on the beach, and the two-day format gives you a short run to bring family to.
Don't pick it for a personal best. Humidity and hills are part of the course, and the September date falls in the wet season on the Andaman coast.
This review is compiled from the sponsor's account of the 2025 edition and a race report on the 2026 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: Where does the Scenic Half Marathon Krabi start and finish?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the 21 km and 10 km road races started at Krabi Provincial Stadium in Ao Nang and finished at Noppharat Thara Beach National Park. A separate 5 km and 3 km beach run was held the day before along the coastal road at Noppharat Thara Beach.

faqs.question: Who won the Scenic Half Marathon Krabi in 2026?
faqs.answer: Poland's Krzysztof Hadas won the men's elite race on 13 September 2026 in 1:08:57, one second ahead of Ethiopia's Tsegaye Keress. Gemechu Dida of Ethiopia was third in 1:09:15, and Thailand's Jongjaijit Intouch finished fifth in 1:11:04.

faqs.question: Is the Scenic Half Marathon Krabi a fast course?
faqs.answer: Not especially. The 2026 race report describes high humidity and a rolling route with hill sections, which made even the elite leaders start cautiously. The race starts at dawn to avoid the worst of the heat, but plan for tropical conditions.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the 2025 and 2026 editions. Replaces a pre-race preview. The 2026 race report is written in a dramatised style, so only its results and its plain statements about the course and conditions are used. No rating: nothing here is participant evidence.
